title: Quantification of Melatonin and AFMK in Cerebrospinal Fluid by LC-MS/MS
author: Artime-Naveda, Hevia-Sánchez, et al.

steps.title: Synthesize 13C1 melatonin
steps.instruction: Perform the six‑day synthesis of 13C1 melatonin as described, then purify the product by silica gel chromatography to obtain a white solid (≈85 % yield).

substeps.instruction: Stir N‑Acetyl‑5‑hydroxytryptamine (200 mg, 0.92 mmol), potassium carbonate (381 mg, 2.76 mmol) and 18‑Crown‑6 (24 mg, 0.09 mmol) in 10 mL acetone at 20 °C for 20 min.
Add iodomethane‑13C (1.84 mmol) and stir sealed at 15‑20 °C for 5 days.
Remove solvent in vacuo.
Dilute residue with 50 mL ultrapure water and extract three times with 50 mL chloroform.
Wash combined organic phases with 50 mL brine, dry over 1 g MgSO4 for 30 min, filter and concentrate under reduced pressure.
Purify the concentrate on silica gel 60 (230‑400 mesh) using chloroform/methanol 99:1 for ~2 h to obtain the white solid.

steps.title: Synthesize 13C1 AFMK
steps.instruction: Convert 13C1 melatonin to 13C1 AFMK in a photochemical reaction, then isolate the product by sequential column chromatography.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 220 mg 13C1 melatonin in 200 mL dichloromethane/methanol (2:1 v/v).
Add 1 mL dry pyridine and 40 mg Rose Bengal; place flask in an ethanol/dry‑ice bath.
Irradiate with a 400 W halogen lamp for 10 h while stirring under an oxygen‑rich atmosphere (oxygen balloon).
Replace O2 with argon or nitrogen, add 2 mL dimethyl sulfide and allow the mixture to equilibrate at 15‑25 °C for 10 h.
Evaporate the residue in vacuo.
Purify by gravity column (10 mm × 200 mm) on neutral alumina 60 (III); elution with chloroform recovers 110 mg unreacted 13C‑melatonin.
Further purify the main‑product‑free fraction on preparative silica gel with 2 % MeOH/ethyl acetate to obtain 30 mg 13C AFMK.
Elute with 3 % MeOH/dichloromethane to collect 70 mg 13C‑cyclic 3‑hydroxymelatonin (amorphous solid).
Confirm absence of 13C‑cyclic 3‑hydroxymelatonin by TLC (CH2Cl2:MeOH 97:3).

steps.title: Prepare standard stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make all required stock solutions of natural and 13C‑labeled melatonin, AFMK, and 5‑methoxytryptophol in acetonitrile, then aliquot and store at –80 °C in the dark for up to 1 year.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 250 µg/g (1 mg/5 mL) stocks of 13C1 melatonin, melatonin, 13C1 AFMK, AFMK, and 2500 µg/g (10 mg/5 mL) 5‑MT in acetonitrile.

Prepare external standard stocks in acetonitrile: melatonin 1 ppm (20 µL of 250 ppm stock in 4980 µL), AFMK 5 ppm (100 µL of 250 ppm stock in 4900 µL), 5‑MT 1000 ppm (2000 µL of 2500 ppm stock in 3000 µL).

Prepare internal standard stocks in acetonitrile: 13C1 melatonin 1 ppm (20 µL of 250 ppm stock in 4980 µL), 13C1 AFMK 1 ppm (20 µL of 250 ppm stock in 4980 µL), 5‑MT 50 ppm (100 µL of 2500 ppm stock in 4900 µL).
Aliquot each stock, protect from light and store at –80 °C (up to 1 year).

steps.title: Prepare 1 ppm working standards
steps.instruction: Dilute the 1 ppm melatonin, 13C1 melatonin, AFMK and 13C1 AFMK stocks in water:acetonitrile (94.4:5.6 v/v) to obtain separate 1 ppm working solutions.

steps.title: Determine experimental isotopic abundances
steps.instruction: Using the LC‑MS/MS MRM method, measure peak areas for natural melatonin, 13C1 melatonin, natural AFMK and 13C1 AFMK; sum all areas for each compound and divide each transition area by the total sum to obtain relative isotopic abundances.

steps.title: Add standards to CSF samples
steps.instruction: Thaw internal standard solutions on ice, add appropriate volumes to each 100 µL CSF aliquot, and record the weight changes to calculate the exact amount of standard added.

substeps.instruction: Thaw 1 ppm 13C1 melatonin and 13C1 AFMK solutions on ice; verify complete thaw and keep on ice.
Thaw CSF (100 µL) in 1.5 mL tubes, weigh each tube with sample on a precision balance.
Add 30 µL 13C1 melatonin working solution, record weight; add 13C1 AFMK working solution (to reach 0.5 ppb final) and record weight.
Alternatively, thaw 50 ppm 5‑MT, dilute to 500 ppb working solution, add 30 µL, and record weight.
Calculate the mass of each added standard by the difference between successive weighings.

steps.title: Extract melatonin and AFMK by LLE
steps.instruction: Perform a liquid‑liquid extraction of each standardized CSF sample with dichloromethane, collect the organic phase twice, evaporate to dryness, and store the dried extracts at –80 °C (up to 1 month).

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL dichloromethane to the 100 µL CSF sample, vortex 10 min.
Centrifuge at 10 000 g for 5 min at 4 °C; collect the lower organic layer.
Repeat the addition of 500 µL dichloromethane, vortex, centrifuge and collect the second organic layer.
Combine organic layers and evaporate to dryness in a speed‑vacuum at 40 °C for 40 min.
Store dried extracts at –80 °C until reconstitution (max 1 month).

steps.title: Reconstitute extracts and set up LC‑MS/MS
steps.instruction: Reconstitute dried extracts in 50 µL water:acetonitrile (94.4:5.6), prepare mobile phases, equilibrate the column, and inject samples together with blanks and calibration standards.

substeps.instruction: Reconstitute each extract in 50 µL water:acetonitrile (94.4:5.6 v/v); weigh the added volume.
Transfer to autosampler vials with inserts.
Prepare mobile phase A: water with 0.1 % formic acid (adjust pH to 3.5 if needed).
Prepare mobile phase B: acetonitrile.
Equilibrate the LC column with initial conditions (water, 5.6 % ACN, 0.1 % formic acid) until pressure stabilizes and no fluctuations are observed.
Load the sequence: first a blank run, then calibration standards (only for the 5‑MT method), followed by the samples.

steps.title: Acquire and process MS data
steps.instruction: Run the LC‑MS/MS method, then open the data files in Agilent MassHunter Quantitative Analysis 10.1, apply the appropriate quantification transitions, integrate peak areas and export the results to Excel.

substeps.instruction: Open MassHunter Quantitative Analysis 10.1 and create a new batch with all acquired files.
Configure the analysis method using the calibration standards (5‑MT method if applicable) and select the MRM transitions for melatonin and AFMK (or SRM for 5‑MT).
Apply the method to integrate peak areas.
Export the integrated data table to Excel.

steps.title: Calculate concentrations – isotopic dilution
steps.instruction: For each sample, compute relative isotopic abundances, determine molar fractions of natural versus 13C‑enriched compounds by linear estimation, and apply the protocol formula to obtain melatonin and AFMK concentrations expressed in pg/mL.

substeps.instruction: Sum transition areas for each compound and calculate relative isotopic abundances.
Determine molar fractions using linear estimation between experimental abundances and known isotopic abundances of natural and 13C‑enriched standards.
Apply the concentration‑calculation formula (step‑by‑step method details 3) to convert molar fractions to concentrations (pg/mL).

steps.title: Calculate concentrations – 5‑MT internal standard
steps.instruction: Using the 5‑MT internal‑standard method, generate calibration curves, compute the recuperation factor from the measured 5‑MT, and correct melatonin and AFMK concentrations accordingly.

substeps.instruction: Record SIM‑mode transition areas for 5‑MT, melatonin and AFMK; construct calibration curves for each.
Determine the experimental 5‑MT concentration in the reconstituted sample and multiply by the mass of 5‑MT originally added to obtain the experimental 5‑MT mass.
Calculate the recuperation factor = experimental 5‑MT mass / theoretical 100 % recovery mass.
Apply this recuperation factor to the measured melatonin and AFMK concentrations using the provided template to obtain final concentrations.
